title: What should the Celix SBOM describe?
question: What exactly should an Apache Celix SBOM describe, and what does that evidence warrant?
knownBoundary: Celix does not currently make a canonical binary release.
A consumer can change the resolved dependency graph through Conan configuration/overrides.
An SBOM for one resolved graph does not warrant a claim about every downstream Celix configuration.
The captured CycloneDX graph is physical evidence from the PR workflow artifact, not the yet-to-be-implemented safe-default lockfile state.

currentResult.focusClaim: The lockfile and SBOM should describe a documented safe-default dependency state while users remain free to change dependency versions and options.
currentResult.maintainerDirection: pnoltes prefers the documented lockfile + SBOM safe-default option; PengZheng subsequently agreed.
currentResult.openBoundary: The precise relationship among the source release, reference dependency state, vulnerability reports, and a possible maintained development-container artifact remains unresolved upstream.

next: Capture the agreed safe-default conan.lock when upstream implements it.
Compare the lockfile graph to the captured CycloneDX graph and identify any drift.
Treat dependency drift as a factual evidence change rather than silently rewriting the argument graph.
Use a second naturally occurring engineering discussion to test whether the grammar generalizes.
